yes_bar: Clear objective stated, referred to during lesson, linked to classroom activities.
Clear I Do -> We Do -> You Do sequence. Logical flow with transitions.
Most activities directly support the learning objective.
Teacher connects new content to previously taught material.
Content connected to students' lives or local context.
Tasks differentiated for at least 2 ability groups.
Plan followed with minor contextual adaptations.
Key resources used as prescribed in lesson plan.

indicator: Time on Task / Time on Learning
yes_bar: 70-85% on task with efficient transitions.
Structured closure: recap key points, check understanding.
Purposeful mix including application & analysis questions. Open-ended questions dominate. Wait time given.
Uses alternative representations (visual, concrete, analogy). Adjusts teaching to student level.
Specific feedback on what was done well and what to improve. Actionable.
Deliberate strategies: cold call, pair-share, name sticks. Diverse students included.
Students make choices about how to demonstrate learning. Explore multiple perspectives.
Clear routines (entry, transitions, dismissal); minimal disruptions. Expectations clear.
Warm, encouraging tone; mistakes treated as learning opportunities.
I Do -> We Do -> You Do scaffolding visible. Problem-solving and creativity modeled with clear strategies.
Purposeful pair/group tasks with clear roles. Students work towards synthesized solutions.
Taleemabad videos/apps used to support learning objectives.
Self- and peer-assessment structured and purposeful. Students use rubrics to assess work.
Resources and space well-organized for collaborative tasks. Materials accessible.
50-75% actively participating (writing, discussing, solving).
Students applying concepts to new problems (Bloom's Apply/Analyze).
Students discuss content in pairs/groups; academic language used.
Students attempt challenging tasks; some comfortable with mistakes.
Students sustain focus for most of independent work time.
Students actively use materials to solve problems or practice.
Students across ability levels and genders are participating.
Content is accurate; no errors observed.
Key terms used accurately and explained to students.
Anticipates and addresses at least 1-2 common misconceptions.
Explains the 'why' behind procedures; uses multiple representations.
Uses concrete -> pictorial -> abstract (CPA) progression; manipulatives present.
Hands-on activities present; students make predictions and observations.
Teacher models reading strategies (prediction, summarizing, questioning). Balanced approach.
Meaningful connections made to at least one other subject area.
